source: SPM 2026 Trial · Johor (Set 3) · English Paper 2 · Part 3 Q5 · Story, 200–250 words
paragraphs: "Ammar realised the message was the beginning of his adventure…" The yellowed note he had found inside an old glass bottle by the riverbank was no ordinary letter. With trembling hands, he unrolled it under the dim light of his torch.

The hidden message was a riddle that read, "The treasure of Kampung Seri lies beneath the old banyan tree across the river. Only the brave will find it." Bursting with curiosity, Ammar shared the riddle with his best friends, Daniel and Mei Ling, and they decided to set off at dawn.

However, the message put Ammar in grave danger. As he crossed the rickety wooden bridge, a plank snapped and he plunged into the raging river. Furthermore, while searching for the banyan tree, he lost his way in the dense jungle as darkness fell. His heart pounded like a drum as eerie sounds echoed around him.

The experience influenced Ammar to face his fears instead of running away from them. When they finally dug up the rusty box, they found only a note saying that true treasure is courage. Moreover, it taught him and his friends that teamwork can help them overcome any challenge in life. Without Daniel's quick thinking, Ammar would not have survived the river.
From that day onwards, whenever life threw obstacles their way, the trio would remember the banyan tree and never give up.

points.text: write what the hidden message was
explain how it risked Ammar throughout the adventure – risk 1
how it risked Ammar – risk 2 ("throughout" = more than one moment)
how the experience influenced him and his friends to face challenges in life – influence 1

gaps: No example sentence for 'I heaved a sigh of relief when …' and 'To my horror, …': the pack's Universal phrases examples for these were scrambled in the PDF text.

'My heart pounded against my chest as …' and 'A chill ran down my spine when …' have only approximate examples: the ST3 universal answer sentences ('My heart pounded in my chest.' and '… I felt a chill run down my spine as the footsteps came closer.'), not the Universal phrases section.
'In the nick of time, …' example is the essay's Table 1 sentence, which belongs to the Extended Version (marked Extended); the Exam Version does not contain the phrase.
The question's required first line is used as the opening paragraph (in the essay it starts with the given words); the Question Analysis row for it has no C code, so it is not in points.
goodPhrases: rows marked (Extended) (anticipation, at the crack of dawn, in the nick of time, gasping for air, swept away by the strong current) were left out.
